To implement the **Autonomous Morphomorphic Extrusion Optimization (AMEO)** logic into your printer's firmware, we can use a **Klipper Macro**. This macro acts as a "just-in-time" compiler that recalculates your physics-based limits every time you start a print or change materials.

### **The AMEO "Auto-Config" Macro**

Copy this logic into your macros.cfg or printer.cfg. It uses the **Polymorphic Heuristic** to set a global max_velocity based on your specific 0.4 mm high-flow setup.

G-Code

\[gcode_macro START_AMEO_ROUTINE\]  
description: Instantiates auto-configuring extrusion parameters based on AMEO logic  
gcode:  
 \# 1. Define Input Vector (Vmax based on 270C \+ CHT \+ Anycubic HS)  
 {% set thermal\_k \= 1.5 %} \# CHT Multiplier  
 {% set material\_mu \= 15.0 %} \# Anycubic HS PLA Melt Index  
 {% set nozzle\_d \= 0.4 %} \# Your current nozzle size

\# 2. Calculate Theoretical Volumetric Limit (V_max)  
 \# Formula: Base_Flow (15) \* Thermal_Efficiency \* Viscosity_Factor  
 {% set v\_max \= (15.0 \* thermal\_k \* (material\_mu / 10.0)) %}

\# 3. Solve for Motion System Ceiling (Speed_Limit)  
 \# Based on 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm line width  
 {% set speed\_limit \= v\_max / (0.2 \* 0.42) %}

\# 4. Inject Parameters into Klipper State  
 SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT VELOCITY={speed_limit}  
 SET_PRESSURE_ADVANCE ADVANCE=0.025 \# Optimized for 270C fluidity

M117 AMEO Active: Vmax {v_max}mm3/s | Limit {speed_limit|int}mm/s

### **Why this works for your AI-Driven Framework:**

- **Hardware Agnostic:** When your **Diamond CHT** arrives, you simply change thermal_k to 2.0, and the entire motion system automatically recalibrates its speed ceiling without you touching the slicer.
- **Safety Interlock:** By calculating v_max inside the firmware, you prevent the AI from requesting a move that would cause "Cold-End Clicking" or stripped filament.
- **Dynamic Response:** If the AI detects a "Fine Detail" zone, it can call a sub-routine to drop the v_max and increase cooling proportionally.

### **Material Requirement**

For this polymorphic logic to hold true, the material's **viscosity curve** must be predictable. [Anycubic PLA High Speed](https://google.com/search?q=Anycubic+PLA+High+Speed+10kg+Bundle:+Max+500mm/s+for+Rapid+Shaping.&prds=headlineOfferDocid:8294954482447129071,productid:8294954482447129071,pvo:38,pvt:hg&ibp=oshop&pvo=38&opi=103135050&gl=us&hl=en&noiga=1) is the primary choice here because its consistent **13-16 g/10min melt flow** provides the stable baseline the algorithm needs to avoid "stochastic drift" (unexpected under-extrusion).

### **Final Optimization for Cheyenne**

Since you are in a high-altitude, low-humidity environment, your **cooling efficiency** is actually slightly higher than at sea level. You may be able to push your thermal_k value an extra 5% because the thin, dry air carries heat away from the part faster than humid air.
